canonical_statement: Let X_0,...,X_(n-1) be mutually independent centered real random variables on a probability space. If each is almost surely bounded in absolute value by b, b and v are nonnegative, and the sum of variances is at most v, then for every t >= 0 the upper-tail probability of their sum is at most exp(-t^2/(2*(v+b*t/3))).
domain_and_universes: universe u; Omega : Type u; MeasurableSpace Omega; a real-valued Nat-indexed family on Omega; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: for i < P.n, P.X i is almost-everywhere measurable
for i < P.n, P.X i belongs to L2
P.X is mutually independent under P.mu
for i < P.n, integral (P.X i) dP.mu = 0
for i < P.n, abs (P.X i) <= P.bound almost everywhere
sum over range P.n of Var[P.X i; P.mu] <= P.varianceBudget
conclusion: P.mu.real {omega | t <= sum over i in range P.n of P.X i omega} <= exp (-(t^2) / (2*(P.varianceBudget + P.bound*t/3)))
